function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph).
• In cities: 25–35 mph.
• Rural roads: 55 mph unless posted otherwise. | Exceeding by 1–5 mph is a “speeding” offense; >5 mph is “reckless driving.” | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• No “no‑seat‑belt” zones. | Failure can result in a fine and points. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers (0.04 %) and drivers under 21 (0.02 %).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” policy for under‑21 drivers. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Texting while driving is a moving‑violation offense. | Violations carry points and fines. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• At four‑way stops, the first‑to‑arrive goes first; if arriving simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on the right. | Failure to yield can lead to points and fines. | | **School Bus** | • Must stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Vehicles traveling in either direction must stop. | Violations are a moving‑violation offense. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the left lane is occupied. | Reckless or careless lane changes can result in points. | | **Points System** | • Traffic violations accrue points on your driver’s license.
• 4 points in 12 months → license suspension.
• 6 points in 24 months → license revocation. | Points can be reduced by attending a driver‑education course. | | **Parking & Parking Violations** | • Parking in no‑parking zones, fire lanes, or handicap spaces without proper permit is illegal.
• Parking on sidewalks or in front of driveways is prohibited. | Violations can result in fines and towing. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Failure to register or inspect can lead to fines and impoundment. | | **Emergency Vehicles** | • Drivers must yield to emergency vehicles with flashing lights and sirens.
• Must pull over to the right and stop. | Failure to yield can result in points and fines. | | **Special Situations** | • **Towing**: Must have a valid towing permit and follow specific rules.
• **Commercial Vehicles**: Additional regulations for trucks and buses (e.g., weight limits, hours‑of‑service). | Commercial drivers face stricter penalties. | ### How to Find More Detailed Information - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Official website provides statutes, regulations, and downloadable handbooks. - **Texas Transportation Code** – The legal text covering all traffic laws. - **Local County Courts** – For specific case law or recent rulings. Feel free to ask if you need details on a particular law or how to handle a specific situation!
